entries.description: --allow-check-edit without a TTY exits 2 and writes nothing.
With a simulated TTY and paths harness.yaml, a write to harness.yaml is allowed and a write to harness/sensors/checks/unit.sh is refused.
check-integrity passes a diff touching only recorded paths, and fails when an unrecorded protected path is also in the diff.
An expired record (older than 12 hours, or from a previous session ID) is ignored.
The authorisation shows up in --report and in the retro's deterministic section.
A triage fixture that discards 2 of 5 reviewer findings yields dismissedByRole.reviewer = 2 and a dismissed rate of 40%.
A finding that disappears after its file changed is classified fixed. One that disappears with no change to its file stays open.
--backlog without a TTY prints the same output as before this change, locked in by a snapshot test.
The loop entry point marks an auth unit needs-human, runs the next unit to completion, and writes a Needs human handoff entry.
--status prints the effective humanRequired.paths, and a local override changes it.
The README section on paths that need a person explains the default, why harness/** is in it, and how to override it locally.
After npm install, format, lint and types report pass or warn, not skipped.
The Stryker integration test finds at least one survivor, and the finding lands in report.json.
Each tier's summary lists the skipped sensors by name.
